questions.stem: What does the gradient of a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: The gradient of a velocity-time graph equals the acceleration, since gradient = change in velocity / change in time.

questions.stem: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph equals the displacement (distance travelled by the object).

questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph, a horizontal line at 10 m/s indicates that the object is:

options.text: Moving at a constant velocity of 10 m/s

questions.explanation: A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph means the velocity is constant. The gradient is zero, so there is no acceleration.

questions.stem: An object moves at a constant velocity of 8 m/s for 5 seconds. What is the area under the velocity-time graph?
questions.explanation: The area under the graph is a rectangle: area = base x height = 5 s x 8 m/s = 40 m.

questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph, what does a line that slopes downward toward zero velocity indicate?

options.text: The object is moving at constant speed

questions.explanation: A downward-sloping line on a velocity-time graph means the velocity is decreasing, so the object is decelerating (slowing down).

questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph, what does a section below the time axis represent?

options.text: The object is moving in the negative direction

questions.explanation: Negative velocity on a velocity-time graph means the object is moving in the opposite (negative) direction.

questions.stem: To find the distance travelled from a velocity-time graph where the shape is a triangle, you use:
questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is 1/2 x base x height. On a velocity-time graph, this gives the displacement for a period of uniform acceleration from rest.
